key_insight: MIRROR exploits the fact that text, image, and combined views of the same geometry problem can trigger different reasoning strengths, using the best view to teach the others for more consistent multimodal reasoning.
engineering_relevance: For multimodal AI systems, the paper offers a practical training strategy to reduce modality-specific failures and improve reliability on geometry-style visual reasoning tasks.
method: Built ODA-Data: paired geometry problems with text-dominant, image-dominant, and image+text views.
Evaluated the model on all views for each problem and selected the best-performing view as a teacher.
Applied a reverse-KL reinforcement learning objective to align weaker views with the teacher view.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that ODA-Data includes training and evaluation splits for modality-dependent reasoning, and MIRROR improves accuracy and consistency across geometry benchmarks relative to standard RL.
watch_item: The approach depends on having multiple aligned views and a reliable way to identify the best-performing view, which may be costly or less stable on datasets outside geometry.
paper_title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
